description: How an LlmCall is presented to Cedar: asking a model is an act policy may refuse, so the model is the resource and the provider is context. `provider` is optional on the Kind and is dropped when the instance omits it. Spec 011 §11 (KS-7): every act now carries the actor's standing into the context — `identity` says whether the request was signed, and `authority_roots` names the keys its cited authority resolves to. Both are the kernel's own answers, settled before `authorize` runs and recorded on the receipt, so a rule written against them decides on the same facts a reader of the chain will see. The field they replace, `@actor.keyFingerprint`, was a fingerprint the actor asserted about itself and is removed from the grammar. R1-F4 (RC review 2026-09-05): `principal_source` is the gateway's own answer about where the client identity came from (`jwt`, `client_metadata`, `mtls_svid`, `anonymous`), so a rule can refuse an anonymous principal; it says how the gateway got the name, never that the name was authenticated.
